knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says that if contaminated equipment touches a clean or food-contact surface, the worker stops, isolates the items, reprocesses the surface and reports if necessary.
Where a required control is unavailable the worker stops and seeks direction. Designated cloths are kept separate for each zone.
The instruction says to perform hand hygiene at task transitions, to change tools when soiled, and to avoid returning dirty tools to clean surfaces.

practicalCriteria: Identifies relevant hazards, scope and site conditions
Selects and explains suitable controls and methods
Performs the sequence without unsafe contamination transfer
Verifies the outcome and documents exceptions
Escalates situations outside training or authority
passRule: Assessor must observe every safety-critical criterion; any failure requires remediation and reassessment.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 2: Keep toilet and bathroom equipment away from kitchen, food and general areas.
Record of procedure step 5: Keep clean supplies separate from used items during transport.
Record of procedure step 7: Reprocess the affected surface using the approved procedure, and report the breach if site policy requires it.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Change a cloth or tool when it becomes soiled, and do not return a dirty tool to a clean surface.
Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: If contaminated equipment touches a clean or food-contact surface, stop and isolate the affected items.
